notes: DVWA stores its difficulty level per-session, so a fresh login always resets it to 'impossible' (no exploitable bugs). dvwa.yaml's auth.post_login pins it back to 'low' right after login, as part of session setup.

security.php, logout.php, setup.php and vulnerabilities/csrf/ are denylisted during the scan: the first three are state-resetting (security.php/setup.php; a spider that auto-submits a discovered GET form would otherwise reset the security level or database), and vulnerabilities/csrf/ is DVWA's own password-change demo via a GET request -- confirmed in testing, an earlier scan without this denylist entry literally changed the logged-in account's password as a side effect of crawling.

sqli_blind/id and brute/username are also genuinely SQL-injectable at security=low but aren't in `expected` (score.py only grades against this list) -- the engine found both in testing; they're left out here just to keep this answer key focused on the PRD's named 8-endpoint set.
Re-run this same scan at security=impossible to confirm zero injection findings (only passive/app-scope findings should remain).
